name: base-swift
comment: /en-us/shop is DELIBERATELY not a criticalPath here, and adding it back re-breaks the gate. base-swift is content-free (expectedCounts pins EcomProducts 0 and EcomGroups 0), so the Shop PLP has nothing to list: with the TruvioCommerce repository built over an empty catalogue the page answers HTTP 200 carrying an in-page Lucene 'numHits must be > 0' error, and with no repository at all it answers HTTP 200 carrying an empty div. criticalPaths is a 2xx assert, so both states PASS a status check while the page is visibly broken - the exact trap base.contract.json records in repositories.note (gate the PLP on a product count and dw-error == 0, never on HTTP status). The shop path is therefore proven by swift-demo, the edition that carries sample data and a built index, and base-swift proves only what a content-free composition can honestly prove. Measured on DW 10.28.10, v5 e2e.
description: The foundational baseline: the one thing to clone that boots a Swift site. base + surface-swift + theme default, NO sample data and NO feature layers - an empty shop with a complete, themed storefront around it, and the declared placeholder footprint of both layers present, parsed and inert. An EDITION and never a merged layer (V5-PLAN D-C): collapsing base and surface-swift into one would force every headless and DAP consumer to carry the Swift design surface, break base.contract.json as the content-free contract additions bind to, and make base-only unprovable. criticalPaths are expressed under the CULTURE segment, not AreaUrlName: on a single-area host Dynamicweb serves /en-us/ and the decorative AreaUrlName 404s (Foundry 965, 1005). compatAxes names all three axes, so an unmet floor fails this edition instead of warning.
